transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me. Like through the conference room walls, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s off. It’s usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company. It sounds so clear that I’ll answer them, and then realize no one else heard anything.
Have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or other substances recently, or around the time these voices started?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t noticed a connection with anything like that. I don’t think there was some specific substance involved when it started.

Alongside these voices, have you noticed any big changes in your mood—like feeling unusually high-energy, elated, or irritable, or on the other hand, very sad, hopeless, or low—that lasted for days or weeks?
I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed it as a mood thing. I mean, I get upset about what I’m hearing, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had days or weeks of feeling unusually high or really low like that.
How long have you been experiencing these voices and the belief that people are talking about you—has this been going on for a few weeks, or longer, like several months or more?
It’s been longer than a few weeks. I’d say the voices from the walls or my phone have been happening for about three months now.
Since these experiences started about three months ago, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to function at work or in your daily responsibilities?

Yes. It’s been pretty bad. I’m not able to keep up at work the way I used to. I run a division, but lately I can’t reliably make decisions or stay on top of things, and some of the senior staff have sort of stepped in and taken over things I used to handle myself.

At home, it’s similar. My husband has had to take care of most of the household stuff because I either leave things half done or don’t start them at all.

Before these voices started three months ago, did you notice any earlier changes—like feeling more suspicious of others, withdrawing socially, or having unusual beliefs—that may have started even earlier, say four to six months ago?

Yes… looking back, I think it was building before the voices. It’s hard to put an exact start on it, but really it goes back about two years and a few months—around when the company expanded and I was put in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. That’s when things started feeling different.

latest_inference.note: The chronic course (over 2 years of insidious decline preceding overt psychosis, now with 3 months of prominent auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions), absence of substance use, and lack of a sustained mood episode support schizophrenia rather than mood-related psychosis, brief psychotic disorder, or substance-induced psychosis. The functional decline at work and home further supports this diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent auditory hallucinations (voices from walls/phone) and persecutory beliefs (board members plotting against her) for approximately 3 months, with a longer prodromal period of subtle behavioral/functional change dating back over two years. No substance use is implicated as a cause, and no sustained mood episode (manic or depressive) accompanies the psychotic symptoms, arguing against a mood disorder with psychotic features or schizoaffective disorder. The presence of clear positive psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and delusions) with significant occupational and domestic functional decline, in the absence of a defined mood syndrome or identified organic/substance cause, and duration criteria (active symptoms >1 month, with a longer overall course including prodrome) meeting general schizophrenia criteria, supports a diagnosis of Schizophrenia, unspecified (F20.9).
